title: Is the Mesenteric Circulation a Source of Systemic Interleukin-6 During Colorectal Surgery?
text: This study investigates whether the systemic interleukin-6 (IL-6) response following colorectal surgery is linked to the mesenteric circulation. Additionally, tissue samples from resected specimens were analyzed for IL-6 expression through quantitative PCR and immunohistochemistry. Postoperative observations indicated a significant elevation in IL-6 levels in mesenteric venous blood compared to systemic venous blood at 6 hours post-resection (p<0.05). Furthermore, IL-6 mRNA levels were notably higher in malignant tissues than in benign tissues (95% CI: 1.2-2.5 fold increase). Immunohistochemical analysis showed denser IL-6 staining in malignant compared to benign epithelium, suggesting a potential localized origin of IL-6 in colorectal surgical sites.

No significant differences in ferritin content were observed between the subepicardial and subendocardial layers either in the control or ischaemic group. title: Does Growth Factor Signaling Inhibition Directly Lead to Reduced B-NHEJ in Plateau-Phase Cells?
text: The relationship between cell proliferation status and DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair via nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) has been a subject of considerable research. We conducted a controlled laboratory study using human fibroblast cell lines deficient in DNA-PKcs, the catalytic subunit critical for the canonical D-NHEJ pathway. Cells were subjected to serum deprivation to simulate growth factor signaling inhibition and then assessed for B-NHEJ activity using quantitative real-time PCR and immunofluorescence microscopy. However, B-NHEJ activity did not significantly differ between serum-deprived plateau-phase cells and those in an active growth state, suggesting that plateau-phase entry alone may be a substantial factor.
